# 2026; only those years have readings, so the cycle column is the year the
# church year begins (reading_cycle,year).  Days the calendar does not draw
# (the World Day of Prayer, national days) are left out.
# The Agenda of the Evangelical Church of the Augsburg Confession in Slovakia
# (1996) lists for every Sunday and feast the texts of several pericope
# systems; these are its first, the old-church lessons (St: a Gospel, an
# Epistle and a psalm, the same every year; a prophecy where it gives one in
# place of the psalm).  Source: Agenda ECAV 1996, "Perikopy", pp. 308-344
# (a copy at files.vlastnawebstranka.websupport.sk), read October 2026.  The
# 19th Sunday after Trinity's Gospel, printed "Mt 9, 18", is the old-church
# Matthew 9:1-8.  The Sunday of Penitence takes the 10th Sunday's texts, the
# second last and last Sundays those of the 26th and 27th.
# Verse numbers are the Latvian Bible's (the Hebrew numbering); the few the
# source gives in the English numbering are given in it (docs/source-errors.csv)
# The LELB gives for every Sunday and feast two sets of readings: the
# historic one-year series (an Old Testament reading, an Epistle and a Gospel
# the same every year: cycle blank) and a three-year series near the Revised
# Common Lectionary (a psalm and three readings, Years A, B and C as the RCL
# counts them), listed under its own heading.  Source: "Dieva Vārds", lelb.lv (the day pages from Advent
# 2017 to November 2026), read October 2026; where a day's one-year texts
# varied, the most frequent are kept.  The three-year Sundays after the
# Epiphany and after Pentecost follow the RCL by date (the Sundays from
# Septuagesima to Esto mihi take the Epiphany Sundays falling on them, Esto
# mihi the Transfiguration); the Sunday of Eternity takes Christ the King.
